03/17.04.2023
1.
Learned counsel for the parties are present.

2. This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs: -
"i.

For a direction upon respondents to immediately and forthwith pay the amount of compensation guaranteed under order passed in memo no. 1611 dated 15.09.2021 (Annexure-5), so far it relates to the petitioner, passed in pursuance of notice issued Sahay Bara vs The State Of Jharkhand on 17 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195041506/
1 under Section 3H of N.H. Act (Annexure-2) in connection with land acquisition case no. 04/2018-19 wherein the petitioner was asked to collect an amount of Rs.
26,82,464/- as the land of the petitioner being Khata no. 573, Khesra No. 7756,
Thana No. 112 has been acquired by the respondent authorities for the purpose of broadening of the road which has been further increased vide Memo No. 1611 dated 15.09.2021.

entities.text: Sahay Bara vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ii. For a direction upon the respondents to take into consideration the representation given by the petitioner vide representation given by the petitioner vide representation dated 11.11.2022 (Annexure-7) and thereafter take a decision on the representation of the petitioner.

Be further pleased to pass such other appropriate writ/writs, direction/directions,
order/orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had earlier moved this Court along with four other petitioners in W.P. (C) No. 4411/2021 challenging the order contained in Memo No.
1611 dated 15.09.2021 passed by the Additional Collector-cum-Arbitrator under the National Highway Act, 1956 in Misc. Case No. 11/2021, whereby petitioners' objection raised under Section 3-5(G) of the Act, 1956 against determination for compensation for acquisition of the land in question was rejected.

The learned counsel submits that the said writ petition was held to be not maintainable in view of the fact that the petitioners had the remedy to challenge the award under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
The learned counsel submits that thereafter no petition under Section 34 of the Act, 1996 was filed and the petitioner is only interested in getting the awarded amount.

The learned counsel submits that the said awarded amount is not being paid to the petitioner on the ground that the petitioner would be entitled only for an amount of Rs.
17,58,922/- instead of Rs. 26,82,464 in connection with which the petitioner has also approached the Deputy Commissioner, Gumla vide letter as contained in Annexure-7.
4. Learned counsel for the respondents has objected to the maintainability of the present writ petition.
He submits that if the award has become final, it is executable under the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and accordingly, the petitioner has a remedy.
The learned counsel has also submitted that in the earlier writ petition, there were five petitioners and this writ petition has been filed only by one of them.

5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, even if the best case of the petitioner is taken that the award has become final, the petitioner has a remedy through the execution proceedings to get the awarded amount.
The executing court would consider the amount payable to the petitioner and also to the other persons claiming under the award .
There could be other circumstances also for consideration by the executing court.
6. Accordingly, this Court is not inclined to grant any relief to the petitioner as prayed for in the present writ petition.
